text:
Traditional markets are reeling under a dual shock as geopolitical conflicts in the Middle East escalate alongside a severe inflation surge. U.S. annual inflation jumped to a three-year high of 4.2% in May, heavily fueled by rising energy costs as disruptions in the Strait of Hormuz escalate. Following U.S. military strikes on Iranian targets, Iran retaliated by launching missiles toward American bases in Kuwait, Jordan, and Bahrain. This escalating crisis, coupled with threats of strikes on infrastructure, wiped out $1.88 trillion across global assets, depressing the S&P 500 and Nasdaq as investors prepare for a hawkish Federal Reserve rate policy at the June 16–17 FOMC meeting.

This massive risk-off contagion is slamming digital assets, with Bitcoin plunging to an intraday low of $60,892 on June 10. Digital asset outflows have accelerated, pushing the Crypto Fear & Greed Index into Extreme Fear at 9/100, though structural institutional progress continues with CME Group's newly launched Nasdaq CME Crypto Index futures.

Ultimately, this landscape illustrates the tight, friction-free transmission channels between traditional macro shocks and digital markets. High inflation and geopolitical base strikes drive immediate capital flight to cash, dragging down both equities and crypto in tandem, proving that digital assets react directly to legacy liquidity drains rather than acting as disconnected hedges.
